title: Not tested is not failed
statement: In any record of what a student knows, keep what was never tested apart from what was tested and failed.
example: A diagnostic with time for 40 to 60 items samples roughly 20 to 30% of a course's components.
detail: The diagnostic guide in the reading project's knowledge base says a diagnostic should produce a knowledge map with explicit uncertainty that separates components with good evidence from those with little or none, and counts conflating an unassessed component with a failed one among the most common errors in diagnostic systems (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0154-diagnostic-assessment-brainlift.qmd`). With time for 40 to 60 items on a course of hundreds of components, a diagnostic samples roughly 20 to 30% of the domain. The course's routing contract requires diagnostics to handle unassessed knowledge (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0164-g3-v2-feedback-agent-routing.qmd`).

evidence.quote: An unassessed KC is not the same as a failed KC, and conflating the two is one of the most common errors in diagnostic systems.
the map must distinguish between KCs where we have good evidence and KCs where we have little or no evidence.
A diagnostic assessment might have time for 40-60 items. You are sampling roughly 20-30% of the domain.
diagnostics route study under uncertainty and must handle slips, guesses, sampling, grain size, and unassessed knowledge; they are not grades;
counting an ungraded written answer as correct would flatter every accuracy figure it reports.
